abandon.meaning: To leave someone or something behind.
abandon.clue: The sailors had to abandon the damaged ship.

abundance.meaning: A very large amount of something; more than enough.
abundance.clue: There was an abundance of cake at the birthday party.

affable.meaning: Friendly, pleasant, and easy to get along with.
affable.clue: Henry, an affable child, always included anyone who was being left out of the conversation.

antiquity.meaning: Ancient times; or an object that has survived from ancient times.
antiquity.clue: The ancient Greek vase was the museum's most precious antiquity.

arduous.meaning: Difficult, tiring, and requiring a lot of effort.
arduous.clue: Building a brick wall is an arduous task.

assiduous.meaning: Working hard and carefully, and not giving up.
assiduous.clue: Jenny was an assiduous candidate during her election campaign for school captain.

avowed.clue: The boy's avowed ambition was to become an excellent mathematician.

barren.meaning: Unable to grow plants; empty and bare.
barren.clue: Very little could grow on the barren land.

belligerent.clue: The belligerent man began shouting at everyone in the room.

besieged.meaning: Surrounded by attackers; also faced with too many demands or problems.
besieged.clue: The besieged city waited anxiously for help while enemy troops blocked every road.

bewildered.meaning: Very confused and unable to understand what is happening.
bewildered.clue: Mia looked bewildered when she saw the complicated instructions.

choreographer.meaning: Someone who plans the steps of a dance.

composition.meaning: Something made by putting parts together, such as music or a piece of writing.

comrade.meaning: A friend who shares your work or experiences.
comrade.clue: The soldier refused to leave his injured comrade behind.

conscience.meaning: Your inner sense of right and wrong.
conscience.clue: His conscience told him that he should admit that he had broken the window.

contemporary.meaning: From the present time; also living at the same time as someone else.
contemporary.clue: The gallery displays contemporary British art.

conventional.meaning: Following the usual way of doing things.
conventional.clue: They chose a conventional design for their new house.

covet.meaning: To want something that belongs to someone else very much.

coy.meaning: Shy, or not wanting to give much away.

deceive.meaning: To make someone believe something that is not true.
deceive.clue: The dishonest salesman tried to deceive his customers.

demolished.clue: The old factory was demolished to make room for new houses.

destitute.meaning: So poor that you lack basics such as food and a home.
destitute.clue: The charity provides food and shelter for destitute families.

dilapidated.meaning: Old and falling apart because it has not been looked after.
dilapidated.clue: They discovered a dilapidated cottage at the edge of the woods.

diluted.meaning: Made weaker by adding water or another substance.

disarray.clue: After the children had finished playing, the room was in disarray.

disastrous.clue: The expedition had a disastrous ending when a storm destroyed their supplies.

dishevelled.meaning: Looking untidy, especially your hair or clothes.
dishevelled.clue: He looked dishevelled after spending the night sleeping on the train.

dismal.clue: The team gave a dismal performance and lost badly.

disperse.meaning: To scatter or spread in different directions.
disperse.clue: The crowd began to disperse after the concert ended.

drought.meaning: A long time with hardly any rain.

embarrass.meaning: To make someone feel awkward or ashamed.

endeavour.meaning: A determined attempt to do something.
endeavour.clue: Climbing the mountain was a difficult endeavour.

enterprise.meaning: A business, or a project you work hard on.
enterprise.clue: Setting up her own bakery was an ambitious enterprise.

errand.meaning: A short journey made to deliver, collect, or do something.
errand.clue: Mum sent me on an errand to buy some milk.

evident.clue: It was evident from his smile that he was delighted.

explanation.meaning: Something that helps you understand how or why.
explanation.clue: The teacher gave a simple explanation of how the machine worked.

famine.meaning: An extreme shortage of food affecting many people.
famine.clue: The failed harvest led to a severe famine.

fatigue.meaning: Feeling very tired after hard work.
fatigue.clue: After hours of walking, she was overcome with fatigue.

feign.meaning: To pretend you have a feeling or problem.
feign.clue: He tried to feign illness so that he could avoid school.

flamboyant.meaning: Bright, bold or showy in a way that gets noticed.
flamboyant.clue: The actor arrived wearing a flamboyant purple suit.

fleet.meaning: A group of ships or vehicles working together.
fleet.clue: A fleet of fishing boats sailed out of the harbour.

frivolous.meaning: Silly or not very serious or important.

gratitude.clue: He expressed his gratitude to the stranger who had helped him.

gregarious.clue: Mia is gregarious and enjoys meeting new people.

grotesque.meaning: Very strange or ugly, sometimes in a frightening way.
grotesque.clue: A grotesque stone creature was carved above the doorway.

helix.meaning: A spiral shape, like a coil or corkscrew.

hygienic.meaning: Clean and unlikely to cause illness or spread germs.
hygienic.clue: Washing your hands before preparing food is hygienic.

idiosyncrasy.meaning: An unusual habit or feature that makes someone different.

immerse.meaning: To put completely under liquid; also to give something all your attention.
immerse.clue: She liked to immerse herself in a good book.

impudent.meaning: Rude and showing a lack of respect.

inaugural.meaning: The first event or the start of something.

inconspicuous.clue: The spy wore plain clothes to remain inconspicuous.

innocuous.clue: The spider looked frightening but was completely innocuous.

insolent.meaning: Rude and showing a lack of respect.

lament.clue: The villagers lamented the loss of the ancient woodland.

lavish.clue: They prepared a lavish feast for the celebration.

malady.clue: The doctor searched for a cure for the mysterious malady.

matte.clue: She chose matte paint because she did not want the wall to shine.

meagre.meaning: A very small amount, often not enough.

melancholy.clue: A feeling of melancholy came over him as he remembered his old home.

merchant.meaning: Someone who buys and sells things.

meticulous.meaning: Very careful about every small detail.

nauseous.meaning: Feeling as if you might be sick.

nimble.meaning: Able to move quickly, lightly, and easily.

nuisance.meaning: Someone or something that causes trouble or annoyance.

obstinate.meaning: Refusing to change your mind or behaviour.

omen.meaning: A sign people believe tells them what will happen.

oppress.meaning: To use power to treat people cruelly or unfairly.

ordeal.meaning: A very difficult or unpleasant experience.

ostentatious.meaning: Showing off money or importance to get noticed.
ostentatious.clue: He arrived in an ostentatious limousine covered in gold decorations.

palaeontologist.meaning: A scientist who studies fossils and ancient forms of life.
palaeontologist.clue: The palaeontologist carefully examined the dinosaur fossil.

peril.clue: The climbers were in great peril when the storm struck.

perish.meaning: To die or be completely destroyed.

pioneer.meaning: Someone who is one of the first to try or discover something new.

placid.meaning: Calm, peaceful, and not easily disturbed.

polarity.meaning: Having two opposite sides or qualities.

pompous.meaning: Behaving as though you are more important than you really are.

precarious.meaning: Not safe or steady, and likely to go wrong.

prohibit.meaning: To say officially that something is not allowed.

provoke.meaning: To cause a reaction, often by annoying someone.

quaint.clue: We stayed in a quaint cottage in a small village.

quench.meaning: To satisfy thirst or put out a fire.

raiment.meaning: Clothes, especially smart or special ones.

reprimand.meaning: To tell someone off seriously for doing something wrong.

restrain.meaning: To hold someone or something back or keep it under control.

rigid.meaning: Stiff and hard to bend; also unwilling to change.

scanty.meaning: Not much; less than is needed.

scripture.meaning: Writings that a religion considers holy.

seize.meaning: To grab something firmly or take it by force.

sermon.meaning: A talk about religion or how people should behave.

stern.clue: The teacher gave the class a stern warning about their behaviour.

submissive.meaning: Ready to obey without arguing or resisting.

succumb.meaning: To give in; also to die from an illness or injury.

tempestuous.meaning: Full of strong feelings, arguments or violent storms.

tranquil.clue: The garden was tranquil in the early morning.

turbulent.meaning: Full of disorder, conflict or rough movement.

vicarious.meaning: Felt through someone else's experience rather than your own.

virtuous.meaning: Behaving in a good and honest way.

wither.meaning: To dry up or become weak.

wretched.meaning: Very unhappy or in a very poor state.

abode.meaning: A place where someone lives; a home.

absurd.meaning: So silly or unreasonable that it makes no sense.

adhere.meaning: To stick to something; also to follow a rule or belief.
adhere.clue: Everyone must adhere to the safety rules.

advice.meaning: Suggestions about what you could do.

ancient.meaning: From a very long time ago.

apparent.meaning: Easy to see; sometimes, seeming to be true.

banish.meaning: To send someone away from a place as a punishment; to get rid of something.

beck.meaning: A movement that calls someone over. At someone’s beck and call means always ready to do what they want.

brusque.meaning: Speaking or acting in a quick, rather rude way.

calamity.meaning: A serious event that causes great damage or suffering.

caulk.meaning: To fill a gap so water or air cannot get through.

clemency.meaning: Choosing to be less harsh when you have the power to punish.

coax.meaning: To gently persuade someone to do something.

commence.clue: The ceremony will commence at ten o'clock.

complement.meaning: Something that completes or improves something else.

compliment.meaning: A polite expression of praise or admiration.
compliment.clue: He paid her a compliment on her excellent performance.

conceal.meaning: To hide something or prevent it from being seen or known.
conceal.clue: He tried to conceal the present behind his back.

conceit.clue: His conceit made him believe he was better than everyone else.

condemn.meaning: To say strongly that something is wrong; also to find someone guilty.

controversy.meaning: A subject that people publicly disagree about.

deceit.meaning: Tricking someone into believing something untrue.
deceit.clue: His deceit was discovered when the truth came out.

deliberate.meaning: Done on purpose and with thought.
deliberate.clue: Breaking the window was a deliberate act.

derelict.meaning: Abandoned and in very poor condition.
derelict.clue: The children were warned not to enter the derelict building.

despise.meaning: To strongly dislike and have no respect for someone or something.
despise.clue: She despised people who were deliberately cruel to animals.

device.meaning: Something made to do a particular job.
device.clue: The small electronic device measures temperature.

din.meaning: A loud, unpleasant noise that goes on and on.
din.clue: The din from the construction site made it difficult to concentrate.

disclose.meaning: To reveal information that was previously secret or unknown.
disclose.clue: The company refused to disclose the confidential information.

dispute.clue: The neighbours had a dispute over the boundary fence.

distress.clue: The injured animal was clearly in distress.

dwelling.meaning: A house or other place where someone lives.
dwelling.clue: The small dwelling stood beside the river.

economical.meaning: Using money, time or supplies without wasting them.
economical.clue: The small car is economical to run.

elude.meaning: To escape from or avoid someone or something, especially cleverly.
elude.clue: The thief managed to elude the police for several hours.

emerge.clue: A butterfly began to emerge from its chrysalis.

endure.meaning: To put up with something difficult; also to last a long time.
endure.clue: The explorers had to endure freezing temperatures.

evaluation.meaning: A careful judgement of how good or useful something is.
evaluation.clue: The teacher completed an evaluation of the student's work.

exaggerate.meaning: To describe something as bigger, better or worse than it really is.
exaggerate.clue: Do not exaggerate the size of the fish you caught.

extinction.meaning: The state of a species no longer existing.
extinction.clue: Habitat loss can push rare animals towards extinction.

factual.meaning: Based on facts rather than opinions or imagination.
factual.clue: The report was factual and supported by evidence.

fatal.meaning: Causing death, or causing something to fail completely.
fatal.clue: The poisonous bite can be fatal without treatment.

feeble.meaning: Weak and lacking physical strength or effectiveness.
feeble.clue: The elderly man spoke in a feeble voice.

fertile.meaning: Able to grow lots of plants or produce young.
fertile.clue: The fertile soil produced an excellent crop.

flourish.meaning: To grow or do very well.
flourish.clue: The plants began to flourish in the warm sunshine.

grave.meaning: Very serious; also a place where a dead person is buried.
grave.clue: The doctor warned that the patient was in grave danger.

grieve.meaning: To feel or express deep sadness, especially after a loss.
grieve.clue: The family needed time to grieve after their loss.

harbour.meaning: A safe, sheltered place for boats; also to keep a feeling inside.
harbour.clue: The fishing boats returned safely to the harbour.

hasty.meaning: Done too quickly and without enough thought.
hasty.clue: He made a hasty decision that he later regretted.

hindrance.meaning: Something that makes progress difficult or slows it down.
hindrance.clue: The heavy snow was a hindrance to the rescue team.

hoax.meaning: A trick that makes people believe something untrue.
hoax.clue: The supposed sighting of a monster turned out to be a hoax.

ignorant.clue: He was ignorant of the rules and accidentally broke one.

imitate.meaning: To copy someone's actions, behaviour, or appearance.
imitate.clue: The child tried to imitate the singer's voice.

inaugurate.meaning: To start something officially, often with a ceremony.
inaugurate.clue: The mayor will inaugurate the new community centre.

incision.meaning: A cut, especially one made during an operation.
incision.clue: The surgeon made a small incision in the patient's skin.

inferior.meaning: Not as good, or lower in rank.
inferior.clue: The cheaper material proved to be inferior in quality.

inhabitants.meaning: People or animals that live in a particular place.
inhabitants.clue: The island's inhabitants depend largely on fishing.

interfere.meaning: To get involved when your help is not wanted or needed.
interfere.clue: She told her brother not to interfere in her argument.

interrogate.meaning: To ask someone lots of detailed, formal questions.
interrogate.clue: The detectives began to interrogate the suspect.

isolation.meaning: Being apart from other people or things.
isolation.clue: The remote village lived in isolation for many years.

lenient.meaning: Not as strict or harsh as you might expect.
lenient.clue: The teacher was lenient and gave him another chance.

liable.meaning: Likely to do or suffer something; also responsible for it by law.
liable.clue: Drivers are liable for damage caused by their negligence.

linger.meaning: To remain somewhere longer than necessary or expected.
linger.clue: The smell of smoke continued to linger in the room.

lofty.meaning: Very high; also grand or noble.
lofty.clue: The eagle built its nest on a lofty cliff.

majestic.clue: The majestic mountains rose above the valley.

margin.meaning: An edge or border; also the amount between two scores or results.
margin.clue: She wrote a note in the margin of the page.

oblige.meaning: To make someone do something; also to help as a favour.
oblige.clue: The rules oblige everyone to wear a safety helmet.

offend.meaning: To upset or insult someone; or to break a law or rule.

opportunity.clue: She had an opportunity to perform on stage.

painstaking.meaning: Done with great care and effort.

passive.meaning: Letting things happen without trying to change them.
passive.clue: He remained passive while the others argued.

peculiar.meaning: Strange or unusual; particular to a specific person, place, or thing.
peculiar.clue: There was a peculiar smell coming from the cupboard.

perceive.clue: She perceived a slight change in his expression.

perplexed.clue: He looked perplexed by the difficult riddle.

pigment.meaning: A substance that gives colour to something.
pigment.clue: The artist mixed a blue pigment into the paint.

plunder.meaning: To steal goods by force, especially during war or disorder.
plunder.clue: The invaders began to plunder the abandoned town.

pretence.meaning: Making something seem true when it is not.
pretence.clue: He made a pretence of being asleep when his mother entered.

proclaim.meaning: To announce something publicly or officially.
proclaim.clue: The king stood before the crowd to proclaim the good news.

prophecy.meaning: A statement that predicts what will happen in the future.
prophecy.clue: According to the ancient prophecy, a great leader would arise.

relevant.meaning: Connected to what you are talking about or doing.

repent.meaning: To feel sorry for something wrong you have done and wish to change.
repent.clue: He began to repent after realising how much harm he had caused.

resort to.meaning: To try something because other ways have not worked.

retreat.meaning: To move back, often away from danger.

rowdy.clue: The rowdy crowd disturbed the neighbours.

sanguine.meaning: Hopeful and confident that things will go well.
sanguine.clue: She remained sanguine about her chances of success.

sanitary.clue: The kitchen must be kept sanitary at all times.

stationary.clue: The car remained stationary at the traffic lights.

sturdy.meaning: Strongly built and unlikely to break or be damaged.
sturdy.clue: The sturdy table easily supported the heavy boxes.

subdued.meaning: Quieter or less bright or strong than usual.
subdued.clue: The usually cheerful class was subdued after hearing the bad news.

subterfuge.meaning: A trick used to hide what you are really doing.
subterfuge.clue: He used subterfuge to conceal his true intentions.

subterranean.clue: The explorers discovered a subterranean tunnel.

summit.meaning: The top of a mountain; also a meeting of leaders.
summit.clue: The climbers finally reached the summit before noon.

superfluous.meaning: More than is needed or necessary.
superfluous.clue: Remove any superfluous details from your answer.

torment.meaning: Severe physical or mental suffering; or to cause such suffering.
torment.clue: The constant toothache was a source of torment.

trivia.meaning: Unimportant facts or details, often interesting or entertaining.
trivia.clue: The quiz included trivia about famous films.

trivial.clue: They argued over a trivial matter.

unfathomable.meaning: Very difficult or impossible to understand.

unsurpassed.meaning: As good as or better than anything else.

vanish.clue: The magician made the coin vanish.

volatile.meaning: Likely to change suddenly; also turning easily into gas.
volatile.clue: The volatile situation could become dangerous at any moment.

yacht.meaning: A boat used for fun or racing.
yacht.clue: They sailed their yacht along the coast.

yield.meaning: To produce something; also to give way or give in.

tardy.meaning: Late; not arriving or happening on time

punctual.meaning: Arriving or happening at the correct time
punctual.clue: Maya is punctual and always arrives before the bell.

deteriorate.clue: Without repairs, the old roof will continue to deteriorate.

thrive.meaning: To grow well or do very well.
thrive.clue: Tomato plants thrive in warm, sunny conditions.

imperative.clue: It is imperative that you wear a helmet while cycling.

lout.meaning: A rude, clumsy, or badly behaved person
lout.clue: The lout pushed to the front of the queue without apologising.

viscous.meaning: Thick and sticky, so it flows slowly.
viscous.clue: Honey is more viscous than water.

vicious.clue: The vicious dog snarled at anyone who approached the gate.

gravely.clue: The doctor spoke gravely about the risks of the operation.

boldness.meaning: Confidence and willingness to take risks

fortitude.clue: He showed remarkable fortitude during the difficult journey.

grit.meaning: Courage to keep trying when things are hard.

apprehension.meaning: Anxiety or fear about what may happen

rivet.clue: The storyteller managed to rivet the children's attention.

tedious.meaning: Boring because it is long or repetitive

apathy.meaning: Lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern

veto.meaning: To use your authority to say a plan cannot go ahead.

agitated.clue: The horse became agitated when it heard the thunder.

sanction.meaning: Official permission; also a penalty for breaking a rule.

feud.meaning: A bitter argument that lasts a long time.

savage.clue: The village was struck by a savage storm.

ferocious.clue: A ferocious wind battered the coast.

callous.meaning: Unkind and showing no concern for others

loathe.clue: He loathed getting up before sunrise.

enmity.meaning: Strong dislike between people or groups.

steadfast.clue: She remained steadfast despite pressure to change her mind.

supple.meaning: Flexible and able to bend easily

foam.clue: White foam gathered on the waves near the shore.

froth.meaning: A mass of small bubbles on a liquid

obscene.clue: The editor removed the obscene language from the article.

vulgar.clue: His vulgar joke offended several guests.

cordial.clue: The two rivals remained cordial when they met.

demolish.meaning: To completely destroy a building or structure

facile.meaning: Easy, or seeming too simple to be useful.

cinch.clue: After weeks of practice, the final routine was a cinch.

intricate.clue: The clock contained an intricate system of tiny gears.

programme.meaning: A planned set of activities or events.

pronunciation.meaning: The way a word is spoken, including its sounds and stress.
pronunciation.clue: I listened to the recording to check the pronunciation of 'yacht'.

purpose.meaning: The reason something is done or made.
purpose.clue: The purpose of the poster was to invite people to our play.

queue.meaning: A line of people or things waiting for their turn.
queue.clue: We joined the queue for the museum's dinosaur exhibition.

recognise.meaning: To know someone or something because you have met or seen them before.
recognise.clue: I could recognise my friend's laugh even behind the curtain.

recommend.meaning: To suggest that something is a good choice.
recommend.clue: Which funny book would you recommend for our reading club?

restaurant.meaning: A place where people pay to sit and eat meals cooked for them.
restaurant.clue: We ate lunch at a restaurant beside the river.

rhyme.meaning: A match between the end sounds of words, such as 'cat' and 'hat'.
rhyme.clue: I needed a rhyme for 'moon', so I chose 'spoon'.

rhythm.meaning: A pattern of beats or sounds.
rhythm.clue: We clapped the rhythm while our friend played the drum.

sacrifice.meaning: To give up something valued for a more important reason.
sacrifice.clue: I would sacrifice some playtime to help my friend finish the model.

secretary.meaning: Someone whose work includes organising records, messages and meetings.
secretary.clue: The club secretary sent everyone the date of the next meeting.

shoulder.meaning: The part of the body where an arm joins the torso.
shoulder.clue: The parrot perched on the pirate's shoulder.

signature.meaning: Someone's name written in their own particular way.
signature.clue: The author added her signature inside my book.

simile.meaning: A comparison using 'like' or 'as' to show a shared quality.
simile.clue: We wrote the simile 'as quiet as a sleeping mouse'.

sincere.meaning: Meaning what you say or feel; not pretending.
sincere.clue: His sincere apology showed that he truly regretted breaking the toy.

sincerely.meaning: In a way that shows you really mean what you say or feel.
sincerely.clue: I sincerely hope you feel better soon.

soldier.meaning: A person who serves in an army.
soldier.clue: The soldier helped deliver supplies after the flood.

stanza.meaning: A group of lines forming a section of a poem.
stanza.clue: The poem had three stanzas; each stanza contained four lines.

stomach.meaning: The organ that receives food after it is swallowed and helps digest it.
stomach.clue: Food travels from your mouth down a tube to your stomach.

structure.meaning: The way the parts of something are arranged.
structure.clue: We planned the structure of our story before writing its opening.

sufficient.clue: We have sufficient paper for everyone to make a kite.

suggest.meaning: To put forward an idea for someone to consider.
suggest.clue: I suggest we name our cardboard robot Sir Rusty.

summarise.meaning: To give the main points in a shorter form.
summarise.clue: Please summarise the chapter in three sentences.

symbol.meaning: A mark, object or sign that represents something else.
symbol.clue: The dove is often used as a symbol of peace.

system.meaning: A set of connected parts that work together.
system.clue: The school's heating system keeps the classrooms warm.

temperature.meaning: A measure of how hot or cold something is.
temperature.clue: We used a thermometer to check the temperature of the water.

theme.meaning: A central idea explored in a piece of writing or art.
theme.clue: Friendship is a theme in the story about two lost penguins.

tone.meaning: The attitude or feeling shown by someone's voice or writing.
tone.clue: Her cheerful tone made the invitation sound welcoming.

twelfth.clue: I was twelfth in the line, with eleven people ahead of me.

variety.meaning: A range of different things or types.
variety.clue: The picnic included a variety of fruit, from apples to mangoes.

vegetable.meaning: A plant or part of a plant used as food, especially in savoury meals.
vegetable.clue: We each chose a vegetable to add to the soup.

vehicle.meaning: Something used to transport people or goods, such as a car or bus.
vehicle.clue: The delivery vehicle stopped outside the bakery.

resolute.clue: Even when the storm made them seasick, the captain kept the boat on its course.

taciturn.meaning: Saying very little; reserved in speech.
taciturn.clue: The old lighthouse keeper was so taciturn that he only ever answered yes or no.

tenacious.meaning: Holding on firmly and refusing to give up.
tenacious.clue: The little plant was tenacious, holding on to the crack in the wall long after the others had died.

apprehensive.meaning: Worried and uneasy that something bad may happen.
apprehensive.clue: Nell lay in bed apprehensive about the storm she could hear outside.

intrepid.meaning: Fearless and willing to take risks.
intrepid.clue: The young explorer was intrepid, climbing the tower in the dark to see the view.

ascend.clue: The kite began to ascend as the wind caught its tail.

meander.meaning: To follow a winding course without a fixed direction.
meander.clue: The path meanders past the barn and the pond before it reaches the village.

propel.meaning: To drive or push something forward.
propel.clue: The rocket engine will propel the balloon higher than the birds.

scurry.meaning: To move quickly in short steps.
scurry.clue: When the cat appeared, the mice scurry back towards their hole.

trudge.meaning: To walk slowly with heavy steps.
trudge.clue: The walkers had to trudge the final mile through the wet mud.

abundant.meaning: Existing or available in large quantities.
abundant.clue: The hedgerow was abundant with blackberries this year.

opulent.meaning: Expensive and luxurious in a showy way.
opulent.clue: The opulent hall had velvet curtains and a marble staircase.

porous.meaning: Full of tiny holes that liquids or air can pass through.
porous.clue: Water dripped through the porous rock and gathered in the cave below.

abhorrent.clue: The smell from the old bin was abhorrent, so everyone shut the window.

hostile.clue: The hostile watchdog barked at every passer-by until the postman arrived.

heinous.clue: Everyone was shocked by the heinous act of pulling the alarm for a joke.

adversity.clue: Through a long winter of adversity, the family kept the fire burning.

abate.meaning: The fierce wind began to abate, and soon the garden was completely still.
abate.clue: The rain finally began to abate just as the school picnic was due to finish.

abduct.meaning: Nobody ever found the man who tried to abduct her, and the case stayed open for years.
abduct.clue: Two masked men attempted to abduct the postman, who managed to call the emergency services.

aberrant.meaning: His aberrant behaviour puzzled the teachers, because it was so different from his usual calmness.
aberrant.clue: The school counsellor called his behaviour aberrant, as no other pupil reacted so violently to a lost pen.

ablest.meaning: The ablest players are chosen first, because they manage the hardest tasks without any help.
ablest.clue: Though only eleven, my cousin proved the ablest goalkeeper in the county tournament.

abominable.meaning: An abominable excuse is one so bad that nobody could possibly believe it.
abominable.clue: The weather was abominable, so our sports day was cancelled and we sat in the dining hall instead.

abomination.meaning: She called the polluted river an abomination and demanded that the factory be shut down.
abomination.clue: Everyone agreed that the amount of litter left in the park after the festival was an abomination.

abrasive.meaning: An abrasive surface feels rough and rubs away at anything it touches.
abrasive.clue: The kitchen sponge was abrasive enough to polish a dirty pan, but far too rough for washing my face.

absence.meaning: The absence of the projector meant that the whole lesson had to be done from the board.
absence.clue: Your absence from Tuesday's rehearsal will mean losing your place in the choir, so tell the director today.

absolute.meaning: With a fever of forty degrees, the doctor's word was absolute: stay in bed.
absolute.clue: There was absolute silence in the hall as the head teacher read out the examination results.

absorbed.meaning: He was so absorbed in building his model railway that his tea went cold beside him.
absorbed.clue: She was absorbed in her new novel and did not hear the bell, or her mother calling her for tea.

abstract.meaning: His explanation of time travel was hard to follow because it was so abstract.
abstract.clue: The pupils found the lesson abstract, as they were asked to argue about a city that does not exist.

abstruse.meaning: The guidebook was written in such abstruse language that we had to guess its meaning.
abstruse.clue: Most of us needed a diagram, because the explanation of the theory was too abstruse to take in at once.

accessible.meaning: Please make your slides accessible, so that everyone in the class can follow them.
accessible.clue: The school website is accessible from any device, and the reading room is open to all students.

acclaim.meaning: Nobody expected the first years' play to win acclaim, and the cast were thrilled with the reviews.
acclaim.clue: The young violinist received acclaim after her solo at the county concert, and everyone asked for an encore.

accolade.meaning: Winning the school writing competition was a real accolade, and everyone was proud of her.
accolade.clue: Receiving a gold medal at the swimming gala was the greatest accolade of her school career so far.

accumulate.meaning: Leaves accumulate in the gutters during autumn and must be cleared before winter.
accumulate.clue: Dust had accumulated thickly on the old piano, and a stack of unopened post lay on the shelf.

accusatory.meaning: The way she spoke made him feel like a criminal, as if she were certain he had taken the money.
accusatory.clue: When he asked about the missing homework, Jordan's tone was so accusatory that her friend stopped talking.

accuse.meaning: Nobody could accuse Maya of missing a single rehearsal, not even in the busiest week of the year.
accuse.clue: The head teacher refused to accuse anyone of cheating until the exam papers had been checked again.

accustom.meaning: Riding a bike to school would accustom the children to busy roads, so we start on a quiet street.
accustom.clue: It took several weeks to accustom the new starters to school life, and one girl still arrives far too early.

acerbic.meaning: The review was acerbic, calling the film dull and the actors wooden, in only three lines.
acerbic.clue: His acerbic reply made the whole class laugh, though the teacher winced at its cruelty.

acquaint.meaning: The new pupil will soon acquaint herself with the staff, as she is friendly and outgoing.
acquaint.clue: You should acquaint yourself with the library rules before borrowing your first book this term.

acquiescence.meaning: The committee's silence was treated as acquiescence, so the decision passed without a single vote.
acquiescence.clue: His acquiescence went no further than a shrug, and he refused to help plan the event.

acquire.meaning: Babies acquire their first words by listening long before they learn to speak clearly.
acquire.clue: You can acquire a lot of confidence by joining the school choir and singing in front of others.

acrimonious.meaning: Their acrimonious argument over the swimming rota lasted the whole of Friday afternoon.
acrimonious.clue: The meeting turned acrimonious after ten minutes, and two committee members walked out shouting.

acronym.meaning: The acronym BBC is spoken as three separate letters, not as a single word.
acronym.clue: The instructions were packed with acronyms, so the coach explained each one before the foreign trip.

adamant.meaning: Despite the rain, the captain was adamant that the match would go ahead as planned.
adamant.clue: She was adamant about wearing trainers to the ceremony, despite all the arguments from her parents.

address.meaning: Never address the head teacher by her first name, however friendly she seems.
address.clue: Please address your questions to the head teacher, as she deals with the bus route.

adequate.meaning: The food was barely adequate, so the class stopped at the bakery on the way home.
adequate.clue: The shelter offers adequate room for forty people, but there is not enough parking nearby.

adherent.meaning: Her essay began with the words of an adherent of peace, and the whole room listened.
adherent.clue: Every adherent of the cycling club must attend the safety talk before borrowing a bike.

adjacent.meaning: The houses adjacent to the school always have heavy traffic at half past eight.
adjacent.clue: Our classroom is adjacent to the library, so we can borrow books between lessons.

adjourn.meaning: Because the lights failed, the judges adjourned the competition and returned the next morning.
adjourn.clue: The match was adjourned when the fog closed in, and the teams went home disappointed.

admirable.meaning: Their admirable fundraising raised over two thousand pounds for the local hospital.
admirable.clue: It was admirable that Priya stayed behind to clear up after the storm, though she was exhausted.

admission.meaning: My uncle paid a small admission charge so that we could see the rare coins on display.
admission.clue: The museum charges no admission fee for pupils, but you must book a place online.

admonish.meaning: His mother admonished him gently about his late nights, and he promised to change.
admonish.clue: The referee admonished the striker for a foul tackle, and a yellow card followed seconds later.

adopt.meaning: The cat was adopted from the shelter after a handwritten advert appeared in the local paper.
adopt.clue: His parents agreed to adopt the rescue puppy, and he chose a name for him on the first night.

adore.meaning: He adores his baby brother and refuses to let anyone else carry him downstairs.
adore.clue: My sister adores her violin teacher and practises faithfully for an hour every evening.

adulation.meaning: The young violinist waved away the adulation and thanked her parents rather than the judges.
adulation.clue: Squads of photographers waited for the winner, offering adulation with every smile and handshake.

advance.meaning: The deadline was brought forward, so the team had to advance their plans by a week.
advance.clue: Reading daily will advance your writing, so the library runs a quiet club at lunchtime.

adversary.meaning: She faced a determined adversary in the final of the chess tournament and won after two hours.
adversary.clue: Our adversaries from the neighbouring school made the final match exhausting, and neither team could rest.

aesthetic.meaning: He chose plain stationery for aesthetic reasons, disliking anything bright or noisy.
aesthetic.clue: The building is admired for its aesthetic qualities, though the heating barely works in winter.

affectionate.meaning: The affectionate note left in her lunchbox said she was thinking of her father.
affectionate.clue: Her affectionate greeting with a gentle hug made everyone in the room feel welcome that afternoon.

affinity.meaning: His affinity with younger children led him to volunteer at the after-school club.
affinity.clue: She has an affinity for old maps, spending hours tracing coastlines in the library atlas.

affirmation.meaning: He gave a firm affirmation of his loyalty, which satisfied everyone in the room.
affirmation.clue: Her affirmation of the plan was recorded in the minutes, and nobody voted against it.

affliction.meaning: Doctors treated the affliction for months before her headaches finally eased.
affliction.clue: A bad tooth caused her such affliction that she missed the whole school trip.

affluent.meaning: They live in an affluent suburb where every driveway holds two cars and a bicycle.
affluent.clue: The affluent family paid for three laptops so that each child had one at home.

affront.meaning: Leaving her out of the team photograph on purpose was a deliberate affront.
affront.clue: She considered his curt remark at the party an affront, and she left the room without a word.

aggressor.meaning: The aggressor knocked a shelf of beakers off the laboratory bench during the argument.
aggressor.clue: The aggressor in the fight was suspended for a week, and the other boy received a caution.

aghast.meaning: My mother was aghast when she saw the state of the car after the concert.
aghast.clue: The whole class was aghast when a window shattered two centimetres from someone's head.

agnostic.meaning: He described himself as agnostic, unsure whether anyone could prove a creator exists.
agnostic.clue: When asked about religion at the fair, the scientist calmly said she was agnostic and left it there.

agreeable.meaning: The plan sounded agreeable, so she raised no objection at the meeting.
agreeable.clue: Our new neighbour was agreeable about the fence, and soon both families were sharing a barbecue.

akin.meaning: When something is described this way, it has almost the same qualities as something else.
akin.clue: Her brother's handwriting is akin to a famous author's, with the same looping letters and heavy pressure.

alacrity.meaning: This describes the speed and cheerful keenness with which somebody gets started on a task.
alacrity.clue: He accepted the invitation with such alacrity that he had his coat on before she had finished talking.

albeit.meaning: You use this word when something is true but does not completely cancel out the point you have just made.
albeit.clue: The climb was exhausting, albeit the view from the top was worth every single step.

alert.meaning: Someone who is this way is wide awake, careful and ready to notice anything important around them.
alert.clue: Stay alert on the stairs, particularly when you are carrying a tall stack of books.

alienate.meaning: If you do this to somebody, you make them lose friends or feel that they no longer belong.
alienate.clue: Rude remarks at the meeting can alienate a whole class, so teachers often warn pupils beforehand.

allay.meaning: You do this to a fear or a worry when you say or do something that takes the edge off it.
allay.clue: A warm drink and a quiet story helped allay her terror of the storm outside.

allegation.meaning: It is something a person says about another, which may well turn out to be untrue.
allegation.clue: The report examined every allegation carefully before deciding that the coach had done nothing wrong.

alleviate.meaning: If something does this to a pain or a hardship, the bad situation becomes a little easier to bear.
alleviate.clue: A warm compress and plenty of rest can alleviate the pain of a sore knee after a long match.

allot.meaning: To do this to something is to share it out, giving each person the part that has been set aside.
allot.clue: The head teacher allotted ten minutes to each group for the final question and answer session.

alluring.meaning: Something with this quality tempts you strongly, usually by looking or sounding wonderful.
alluring.clue: The travel agent used alluring photos of beaches and night markets to sell the package holiday.

allusion.meaning: A writer who does this mentions something briefly and a famous story or person comes to mind.
allusion.clue: Her speech contained a clear allusion to the Trojan horse, and half the audience smiled.

ally.meaning: This person or country stands beside you and offers help, especially when things are hard.
ally.clue: At the hearing, her ally stood up and explained exactly what had happened that afternoon.

altercation.meaning: It is a short, heated disagreement between two people, often over something trivial.
altercation.clue: A noisy altercation in the corridor made the teacher send both boys back to their lessons.

altitude.meaning: This tells you how high a place or object sits above the ground or above the sea.
altitude.clue: The mountain guide checked the altitude of the path before the group began the long climb.

altruistic.meaning: A person who behaves this way gives time, money or help to others simply because it is right.
altruistic.clue: Giving up her Saturday to run the charity cake stall, she was quietly altruistic in every way.

ambition.meaning: This is the strong drive a person feels to reach a difficult goal in work, sport or study.
ambition.clue: Her ambition to become a surgeon led her to spend every holiday shadowing doctors at the hospital.

ambivalence.meaning: Someone who feels this is torn between two options and cannot decide which one to choose.
ambivalence.clue: Her ambivalence about choosing between medicine and design meant the choice took weeks longer.

amend.meaning: To do this to a law or rule is to change some of its wording so that it works better.
amend.clue: The committee voted to amend the rule so that pupils could use phones in the dining hall.

amiable.meaning: A person with this quality is warm and cheerful to be with, so nobody feels nervous nearby.
amiable.clue: The new head teacher was so amiable that nervous first years settled into school within days.

amorphous.meaning: A shape with this quality has no clear outline, and a plan with it has no clear detail.
amorphous.clue: The spilled drink left an amorphous puddle across the worktop, impossible to wipe into neat edges.

amphibian.meaning: It is a creature like a frog or a newt that lives part of its life in water and part on land.
amphibian.clue: An amphibian needs damp skin, which is why the class kept the classroom tank shaded.

ample.meaning: If something is this, there is plenty of it and nobody is going to run short.
ample.clue: There was ample time before the bell, so the class began its history project without hurrying.

amusing.meaning: It describes something funny and light-hearted that people enjoy hearing or watching.
amusing.clue: The class clown's imitation of the head teacher was so amusing that the whole room burst out laughing.

anagram.meaning: Every letter of the original is kept, but the letters are shuffled to make a new word.
anagram.clue: In the puzzle, she had to find an anagram of 'silent', which uses exactly the same five letters.

analogy.meaning: This explains something by showing how it is the same as something else the reader already knows.
analogy.clue: The teacher drew an analogy between a cell and a busy city, where the nucleus ran everything.

anarchist.meaning: They want to get rid of government and rules, believing people should organise themselves freely.
anarchist.clue: In the novel, a character is called an anarchist because he believes every rule should be destroyed.

ancestral.meaning: A habit or possession with this quality has been handed down through many generations of a family.
ancestral.clue: The old ring was ancestral, handed down from grandmother to mother and then to my cousin.

anecdote.meaning: It is a short personal story you tell to make a point or to amuse a group of people.
anecdote.clue: He opened his talk with a short anecdote about two cyclists hiding in a farmyard barn.

angst.meaning: This is a heavy, nervous feeling of fear about what might happen or go wrong.
angst.clue: Waiting for the exam results filled him with such angst that he could not sleep for days.

antagonistic.meaning: Such a person argues constantly and treats every other view as something to be beaten.
antagonistic.clue: He became antagonistic whenever anyone questioned him, so meetings turned into long arguments.

antidote.meaning: It is given to a person who has taken poison in order to make that person safe again.
antidote.clue: The paramedic used an antidote straight away, undoing the effects of what he had swallowed.

antipathy.meaning: The feeling is so strong that somebody will avoid the person or the thing altogether.
antipathy.clue: Her antipathy to all insects grew so strong after a bee sting that she left the room.

antiquated.meaning: It belongs to an earlier age and is now judged to be behind the times.
antiquated.clue: Our cellar holds an antiquated box of equipment from the last century, including a horn for gramophone records.

antithesis.meaning: Two things set side by side like this could hardly be more different from each other.
antithesis.clue: In her essay she used a striking antithesis, placing kindness beside cruelty to show how far apart they are.

anxious.meaning: You cannot settle down, and you keep worrying about what might go wrong.
anxious.clue: She became anxious before the reading assessment, checking her watch and the clock again and again.

aperture.meaning: Light passes through this small hole, for example the adjustable opening inside a camera lens.
aperture.clue: The photographer narrowed the aperture slightly, so only a thread of light reached the film.

aphorism.meaning: It is brief and memorable, and it sums up a piece of advice or a piece of general wisdom.
aphorism.clue: His coach's aphorism about hard work beating clever shortcuts stayed with the team for months.

apoplectic.meaning: The person is not merely annoyed but shaking with rage and almost unable to speak.
apoplectic.clue: When he saw his name missing from the team sheet, he was so apoplectic that he could barely speak.

appeal.meaning: You do this when you ask the people who made a decision to examine the case again.
appeal.clue: Her parents made an appeal to the exam board, asking them to look at the marking again.

appearance.meaning: This covers how you look, including your clothes and the way you carry yourself.
appearance.clue: She changed her appearance for the class photograph, choosing a crisp white shirt and a red bow tie.

appease.meaning: You do this when you give in to an angry person or do something to calm them down.
appease.clue: To appease the furious crowd, the caretaker turned down the music and opened the windows.

appetising.meaning: It smells or looks so delicious that you feel hungry the moment you notice it.
appetising.clue: The smell of cinnamon and orange from the kitchen was so appetising that the class was ravenous at once.

apprentice.meaning: A beginner takes the job for a while and learns the skills from someone already skilled.
apprentice.clue: For two years he worked as an apprentice in a bakery, learning to bake under the head baker.

apprise.meaning: Somebody makes certain that you find out about it, often in writing.
apprise.clue: A letter went home to apprise parents of the change, as the term will now finish a week earlier.

approve.meaning: You give your agreement to it and allow it to go ahead.
approve.clue: The governors approved the idea of a talent show and gave the pupils a slot in the hall.

apt.meaning: It suits the situation perfectly, like a comment that could not have been better chosen.
apt.clue: The teacher praised her short phrase because it was an apt answer to that tricky old riddle.

aptitude.meaning: It is something you seem to be born with, rather than a skill you had to practise.
aptitude.clue: She showed a real aptitude for numbers, solving the hardest puzzle in minutes without any help.

arbitrary.meaning: The choice was made for no particular reason, so a different one could just as easily have happened.
arbitrary.clue: Choosing which team plays first is arbitrary, since the names are simply drawn out of a hat.

archaic.meaning: The words or customs in it come from long ago and sound strange to people today.
archaic.clue: The poem uses archaic expressions like 'thee' and 'hath', which no one would say in a text message today.

architecture.meaning: It is the design of the building, and the style that the person who designed it chose.
architecture.clue: The class studied the architecture of the old cathedral, admiring its clever arches and tall stone towers.

ardour.meaning: If you have ardour for a cause, you care about it so deeply that you want to give all your energy to it.
ardour.clue: Her ardour for the school choir was so strong that she practised the same difficult song every evening.

argument.meaning: When two people hold different opinions and argue, that clash between their views is called an argument.
argument.clue: The class had a lively argument about whether the sports day should be moved, and the head teacher settled it.

arouse.meaning: Something unexpected and loud can arouse your curiosity, making you want to find out more about it.
arouse.clue: The mysterious noise in the old shed aroused her curiosity, so she told her friends about it.

arrogance.meaning: A person who believes they are cleverer and more important than everyone else is showing arrogance.
arrogance.clue: His arrogance annoyed the rest of the team, because he refused to listen to anyone's ideas.

artful.meaning: Someone artful uses flattery and tricks to reach their goal rather than being open about their aims.
artful.clue: The artful salesman praised everything we owned so that we would buy his useless old car.

article.meaning: On a form, each different part listed separately is counted as an article of clothing or equipment.
article.clue: The museum guide pointed to a golden article from ancient Rome and explained why it was so rare.

articulate.meaning: An articulate pupil can explain her thinking out loud so that everyone understands exactly what she means.
articulate.clue: The youngest pupil gave an articulate account of her project, speaking clearly and answering every question confidently.

artificial.meaning: Anything artificial has been designed by human hands, even when it copies a flower, a voice or a piece of fruit.
artificial.clue: The artificial flowers in the hall looked so convincing that several visitors asked where they were bought.

artisan.meaning: Every plate in the exhibition was created by an artisan, who shaped and decorated it entirely by hand.
artisan.clue: A local artisan came to school to show us how she makes clay pots on a spinning wheel.

ascendancy.meaning: After being elected, the new captain's ascendancy over the team was complete, and every decision was his.
ascendancy.clue: The team's ascendancy during the tournament was remarkable, winning eleven matches out of twelve.

ascent.meaning: Going up the steep path was tiring, so the walkers stopped twice to catch their breath.
ascent.clue: During their ascent of Snowdon, the hikers battled against strong winds and thick cloud.

ascetic.meaning: For many months the ascetic monk ate only bread and vegetables and refused every comfort.
ascetic.clue: The ascetic's simple life gave him a calm that our busy household could hardly imagine.

askance.meaning: When someone looks askance, their expression warns you that they are doubtful about what they are seeing.
askance.clue: The head teacher glanced askance at the timetable, clearly suspecting that somebody had made a mistake.

aspiration.meaning: Her wish to become a surgeon grew from the day her grandmother recovered after a serious illness.
aspiration.clue: Their aspiration to build a new library for the village finally succeeded after three years of writing letters.

assemble.meaning: All the pupils assembled in the hall at lunchtime to hear the announcement about the trip.
assemble.clue: The whole school assembled in the playground, waiting quietly for the visitors to arrive.

assertive.meaning: She was assertive at the parents' evening, calmly explaining why the trip needed another week of planning.
assertive.clue: Rather than agreeing to everything, the pupil was assertive and told the group fairly what she thought.

asset.meaning: A person who helps a team in a difficult moment is an asset, because the whole group depends on them.
asset.clue: Her calm manner during the reading test was a real asset, because the class settled at once.

assistance.meaning: With a little assistance from a reading volunteer, the youngest boy finished his work before the bell.
assistance.clue: The school offered free assistance with homework to every pupil who came to the Tuesday club.

assortment.meaning: The shop window held a mixture of biscuits, from plain digestives to chocolate ones packed in red foil.
assortment.clue: Each stall at the fair sold a different assortment of cakes, and the queue reached the car park.

assuage.meaning: Nothing the doctor said could calm the boy's fear about the operation the following week.
assuage.clue: A gentle hug from her mother helped assuage the little girl's worry when the thunder began again.

astonishment.meaning: To the astonishment of everyone in the room, the shyest boy stood up and gave his opinion.
astonishment.clue: Her astonishment was obvious when the school cat reappeared after missing for six weeks.

astounding.meaning: Nobody could explain how such a small sample produced such an enormous amount of food.
astounding.clue: It was astounding that the tiny seedling had grown into a tree taller than the classroom door.

asunder.meaning: The gale tore the old fence into pieces, leaving splinters scattered across the garden lawn.
asunder.clue: The storm tore the greenhouse roof asunder, and glass lay across the lawn for hours.

atrocious.meaning: The weather on the camping trip was dreadful, with hail hammering the tents throughout the night.
atrocious.clue: His behaviour in the dinner queue was atrocious, and the teacher sent him to see the head.

attempt.meaning: Her effort to break the school record failed, but she had trained hard for it all summer.
attempt.clue: His first attempt at free-throw practice was hopeless, so the coach showed him how to hold the ball.

attentive.meaning: The attendant asked the class to be attentive during the demonstration, because the experiment could not be repeated.
attentive.clue: Always attentive, Aran spotted three spelling mistakes that the rest of the group had missed.

attribute.meaning: People used to blame the noise in the old house on ghosts, though the survey proved otherwise.
attribute.clue: The examiner attributed the delay to heavy traffic, and apologised to the waiting candidates.

audacity.meaning: It took real nerve for the pupil to ask the head teacher such an awkward question in front of everyone.
audacity.clue: The reporter had the audacity to knock on the headmaster's door during assembly and request an interview.

audition.meaning: At the audition, each child read a short poem to find out whether he could join the play.
audition.clue: Nervous at first, Sofia sang beautifully in her audition and was given the part of the queen.

augment.meaning: The school added extra books to its reading scheme so that every class had fresh titles each term.
augment.clue: Extra vegetables augmented the meal, and the hungry footballers asked for seconds straight away.

autonomous.meaning: The older pupils work independently, so they organise their own homework in the study room.
autonomous.clue: As an autonomous learner, Priya planned her revision timetable and needed almost no reminders from her parents.

aversion.meaning: He cannot stand getting his hands dirty, so he always wears gloves in the garden.
aversion.clue: Her aversion to public speaking faded after she gave a short talk to her own class.

avoid.meaning: You should keep away from running in the corridor, because someone could be seriously hurt.
avoid.clue: The pupils avoided the wet grass by walking round the edge of the field instead.

awe.meaning: The children stared in wonder at the huge whale skeleton hanging from the museum ceiling.
awe.clue: Visitors to the cathedral looked in awe at the painted ceiling, which took six years to finish.

awry.meaning: Her essay went wrong when the computer crashed and half of it disappeared.
awry.clue: The picture on the wall hung awry, so the caretaker adjusted it carefully before the visitors arrived.

axiom.meaning: He treated the rule about uniform as an axiom, though it had never actually been voted on.
axiom.clue: For years the family followed the old axiom that money should never be discussed at the table.

baleful.meaning: The witch cast an evil look at the children, who clutched their bags a little tighter.
baleful.clue: He gave his brother a baleful stare after the prize had gone to someone else.

balk.meaning: The horse stopped at the steep bank, so the rider had to lead it the long way round.
balk.clue: Several boys balked at swimming in the cold water, and asked to watch instead.

banal.meaning: The speech was so predictable that every pupil fell asleep, and nobody wrote a single note.
banal.clue: The holiday programme followed a banal pattern of talks and quizzes, with nothing new to look forward to.

bane.meaning: Rain on the sports day is a real bane, because every teacher ends up soaked and covers muddy.
bane.clue: Missing pens during lessons proved a constant bane, and the class kept a box at the front of the room.

barbarian.meaning: The visitors called the raiders barbarians because they destroyed the paintings for no reason at all.
barbarian.clue: When the crop failed, the hungry crowd behaved like barbarians and broke into the food store.

barricade.meaning: The road was closed with a barricade of wooden crates and paint tins by the residents.
barricade.clue: Rows of benches made a barricade across the entrance, so nobody could get into the hall.

belies.meaning: The figures in the report showed the opposite of the claim that the school had improved.
belies.clue: His tired face belied his claim of having slept for ten hours the night before.

belittle.meaning: She tried to make her brother feel small in front of visitors, which made everybody uncomfortable.
belittle.clue: Constant criticism from the older pupil belittled the beginner, so she stopped volunteering to answer.

bellicose.meaning: The two boys were eager for a fight after the whistle blew, each blaming the other for the foul.
bellicose.clue: Rather than shaking hands, the captains made bellicose speeches that only deepened the quarrel.

bemoan.meaning: He spent the holiday wishing he had brought his bike, instead of going out with his friends.
bemoan.clue: The retired headteacher bemoaned the passing of the old grammar school, which closed in nineteen eighty-four.

bemuse.meaning: Such complicated instructions confused the class, and half of them built the wrong model.
bemuse.clue: The instructions in the booklet bemused me completely, so I asked a grown-up for help.

benefit.meaning: One clear advantage of walking to school is that you get a little exercise before lessons begin.
benefit.clue: Regular revision has a real benefit, and the children who practised scored far better in the maths paper.

benevolent.meaning: The pupils' charitable fundraising raised over two hundred pounds for the local food bank.
benevolent.clue: A benevolent uncle paid for the school trip so that every child could join in.

benign.meaning: The doctor said the lump was harmless, which meant that no treatment was needed at all.
benign.clue: Doctors reassured the family that the growth was benign and would disappear on its own.

bequeath.meaning: Bequeathing a gift means arranging, in advance, for it to become somebody else's property after the giver has gone.
bequeath.clue: In her will, Grandma bequeathed her old piano to my cousin, who had always admired it.

bereft.meaning: Bereft describes a person or place that has lost something precious and now feels strangely empty.
bereft.clue: The old tree stood bereft of its leaves after the fierce storm had torn them away in a single night.

besiege.meaning: When an army besieges a town, it camps outside the walls and cuts off food, water and news.
besiege.clue: For three months the enemy army lay outside, besieging the castle while the defenders grew short of food.

betray.meaning: If you betray a friend, you break their trust and help those who would do them harm.
betray.clue: He promised to keep our conversation secret, yet the name he betrayed to the newspaper was mine.

biased.meaning: A judge who is biased decides in favour of one person, whatever the evidence really shows.
biased.clue: Several parents complained that the judge was biased because he always praised girls and ignored the boys.

bickering.meaning: Constant bickering over tiny things can ruin a friendship that might otherwise be happy.
bickering.clue: By lunchtime the two sisters were bickering again about who had to wash the last cup.

biodiversity.meaning: Hedges and ponds give insects, birds and plants a chance to live, so they increase the biodiversity of an area.
biodiversity.clue: Wildflower verges along the railway track are home to bees and butterflies, so they boost the biodiversity of the whole village.

bipartisan.meaning: A bipartisan committee means members from both main parties are working together on a problem.
bipartisan.clue: The new law was passed after a bipartisan committee agreed on a plan neither side could argue with.

blasphemy.meaning: People thought the film was blasphemous because it made fun of a religion that many viewers follow.
blasphemy.clue: Some worshippers walked out, saying the comedian's joke about their faith was nothing short of blasphemy.

bleak.meaning: A bleak winter afternoon is cold, grey and utterly without cheer.
bleak.clue: The forecast promised a bleak week of rain, so we cancelled the picnic and stayed indoors playing games.

blissful.meaning: After the long ordeal she felt blissful, as if all her worries had floated away.
blissful.clue: He looked blissful on his birthday morning, holding the brand new cricket bat his father had promised.

boisterous.meaning: The children became boisterous the moment the music started and the teacher left the room.
boisterous.clue: A crowd of supporters was waiting outside, chanting and joking in a boisterous welcome for the winners.

bolster.meaning: Extra helpers bolstered the team's defence in the closing minutes of the match.
bolster.clue: Reading every evening bolstered her confidence before the speech she had to give in public.

boon.meaning: The loan was a real boon, allowing the family to repair their leaking roof.
boon.clue: Having a warm kitchen after weeks of cold meals was an enormous boon to everyone at home.

braggart.meaning: The braggart claimed three medals before the results had even been announced.
braggart.clue: Our new boy keeps telling everyone he is the best footballer, which makes some of us roll our eyes.

brawn.meaning: His shoulders were covered with brawn after years of rowing at school.
brawn.clue: The tug of war was decided by pure brawn rather than skill, as the two teams hauled at the rope.

brazen.meaning: Brazen drivers who ignore the red light are a danger to everyone on the road.
brazen.clue: It was brazen of him to walk into the headmaster's office wearing sunglasses and shouting his name.

breach.meaning: Publishing the secret was a breach of trust that could never be repaired.
breach.clue: Students must not read another pupil's diary, because doing so breaches the rules and could lead to punishment.

breadth.meaning: His breadth of knowledge about the subject made him the obvious choice for the team.
breadth.clue: What impressed me about the course was its breadth, from science lessons to music, drama and expeditions.

brevity.meaning: The brevity of her answer showed that she had no wish to discuss the matter.
brevity.clue: Because of the time limit, the speaker's brevity meant he covered only two of the six questions.

brief.meaning: The head teacher gave a brief talk before the results were announced.
brief.clue: We only had a brief moment to grab our books before the bell rang for the next lesson.

brisk.meaning: A brisk walk in the cold air left us warm and wide awake.
brisk.clue: The trainer kept the session brisk, making us run a full circuit of the pitch every minute.

brooding.meaning: He sat brooding over the results, unable to decide whether to apply again next year.
brooding.clue: Since losing the final she has been brooding, staring out of the window and ignoring her friends.

bulky.meaning: The parcel was so bulky that the postman had to push it through the doorway on a trolley.
bulky.clue: Moving house meant carrying a bulky wardrobe up two flights without damaging the paintwork.

burden.meaning: Looking after three younger brothers was a heavy burden for the tired mother.
burden.clue: The extra homework was a real burden that evening, so we asked the teacher for a little longer.

burgeon.meaning: The seedling in the corner of the garden has burst into life during the warm weeks.
burgeon.clue: Sales in the shop burgeon after the new cake appeared on the television programme last week.

bustling.meaning: The bustling market square is packed with shoppers and loud with sellers calling out their prices.
bustling.clue: By nine o'clock the bustling high street was full of commuters, delivery vans and open shop doors.

buttress.meaning: The huge stone buttress takes the weight of the vaulted roof off the medieval wall.
buttress.clue: A wooden buttress was hammered across the gate to stop the battering ram from forcing it open.

cache.meaning: The squirrel's winter cache of nuts is hidden under the roots of the oak tree.
cache.clue: She found a cache of old coins while digging in the garden and showed them to her father.

cacophony.meaning: The school concert raised such a cacophony of noise that the conductor gave up waving his baton.
cacophony.clue: Three bands played different tunes at once and the resulting cacophony made the audience laugh.

cajole.meaning: She cajoled her brother into tidying his room by promising to drive him to the match.
cajole.clue: He cajoled the usher into letting us sit near the front by saying he knew the headmaster.

callow.meaning: The captain was too callow to notice that the other side had changed players.
callow.clue: A callow new prefect kept giving directions to the wrong classroom until an older student helped.

calm.meaning: Stay calm when you are worried, and think before you answer the teacher.
calm.clue: The calm voice of the head teacher soon settled the noisy class after the fire alarm sounded.

campaign.meaning: The school's campaign to save energy was so successful that the bill fell in June.
campaign.clue: Our campaign for a new library has already collected two thousand signatures from parents and pupils.

candidate.meaning: Each candidate was given five minutes to explain their idea for the youth club.
candidate.clue: The interview panel asked every candidate the same question about managing a large team.

candour.meaning: I appreciated her candour in admitting that the plan had not worked.
candour.clue: His candour impressed the judges, as he admitted exactly which parts of the project he could not finish.

canopy.meaning: Under the trees the light is dim, because their leaves make a thick canopy overhead.
canopy.clue: We ate our lunch beneath a canopy of branches while the rain drummed on the leaves.

cantankerous.meaning: A cantankerous old neighbour grumbles at the slightest sound from next door.
cantankerous.clue: Our cantankerous coach blew his whistle twice whenever anyone passed the ball in the wrong direction.

capricious.meaning: The capricious weather gave us a sunbathe in the morning and freezing rain by lunchtime.
capricious.clue: Her capricious nature means she can agree with a plan today and change her mind by breakfast.

careering.meaning: A careering lorry skidded on the wet road and hit the wall at the corner.
careering.clue: Two cars came careering around the bend and nearly collided with our bus.

caricature.meaning: The newspaper caricature made the minister look like a grinning clown with enormous ears.
caricature.clue: The artist drew a friendly caricature of our head teacher to hang in the school hall.

catastrophe.meaning: A fire at the theatre would have been a catastrophe, luckily the alarm sounded in time.
catastrophe.clue: When the tent blew away in the wind, my brother called it a catastrophe, but we laughed.

cathartic.meaning: Writing about her worries proved cathartic, and by Friday she felt much better.
cathartic.clue: The cathartic power of comedy helped us laugh off our worries after the long exam week.

caution.meaning: Drivers should approach the bend with caution, especially when the road is wet.
caution.clue: Because of the slippery rocks, the sign at the river gave a clear caution to the children to keep away from the edge.

cavorting.meaning: The children were cavorting on the grass while the rest of us tried to work.
cavorting.clue: They spent the whole lunch break cavorting across the field instead of finishing their sandwiches.

cease.meaning: The factory will cease production in March, so many workers are worried about their jobs.
cease.clue: The rain had not ceased by lunchtime, and our match was cancelled for the third time.

cerebral.meaning: The film was cerebral rather than action-packed, with long talks about philosophy.
cerebral.clue: Some pupils found the cerebral challenge of the maths olympiad more exciting than a football match.

certitude.meaning: She answered with certitude, even though she had never seen the document she described.
certitude.clue: The witness spoke with such certitude that the jury accepted his account without question.

chameleon.meaning: The little lizard acted like a chameleon, turning green whenever it hopped onto a leaf.
chameleon.clue: A chameleon can flatten its body and change its colour, so predators often fail to spot it.

chaos.meaning: When the storm knocked the power out, the whole street was in chaos for hours.
chaos.clue: Papers, books and half-eaten lunches covered the floor in complete chaos after break.

charismatic.meaning: A charismatic person draws others to them easily and fills a room with energy.
charismatic.clue: Our new headteacher inspires everyone simply by standing in front of the room, even on a Monday morning.

charitable.meaning: Someone who is charitable gives freely to others and expects nothing back.
charitable.clue: My aunt spends every Saturday helping at the soup kitchen, and she never asks for anything back.

charlatan.meaning: A charlatan fools people into thinking they are an expert when they are not.
charlatan.clue: He sold us fake maps, and when we compared them with real ones we realised he had fooled us all.

charming.meaning: Something charming makes everyone feel welcome and happy to be there.
charming.clue: The old bookshop at the end of our high street is full of tiny reading nooks, and everyone who enters leaves happy.

chasm.meaning: A chasm is a huge crack or hollow that is far too wide to jump across.
chasm.clue: There was a sudden drop right in front of us, and sheep were grazing two hundred feet below.

chastised.meaning: Being chastised means being talked to sharply and told off for misbehaving.
chastised.clue: The headteacher dealt with the boys who smashed the window by making them tidy the corridor all week.

cherished.meaning: If something is cherished it matters so much that you look after it carefully.
cherished.clue: My little sister wore her mother's ring every day and guarded it carefully, even in the playground.

chicanery.meaning: Chicanery means using underhand tricks to win something instead of playing fair.
chicanery.clue: The newspaper reported that the contract had been won through underhand methods, and the minister resigned the next day.

citizen.meaning: A citizen has all the rights and duties of someone born in that country.
citizen.clue: Everyone born here can apply for a passport, which shows the country recognises them as one of its own.

clandestine.meaning: A clandestine plan is kept hidden because those behind it do not want it discovered.
clandestine.clue: The film told the story of a spy who met her contacts in hidden places, and her family never found out.

clement.meaning: Being clement means treating a mistake gently instead of punishing it heavily.
clement.clue: The headteacher was gentle with the pupil who had a temperature, and let her finish her test later.

clench.meaning: If you clench your hand you squeeze it into a hard ball to hold on.
clench.clue: He held the handle of his bag so tightly that his knuckles turned white before the swimming race.

cliché.meaning: A cliché is a well-worn expression that now sounds stale rather than striking.
cliché.clue: The essay was full of old lines such as 'raining cats and dogs', which every writer had used before.

clutter.meaning: Clutter is a pile of objects left in the way, so a room feels untidy and hard to use.
clutter.clue: The old garage was full of tools and broken boxes, so we spent all morning clearing it out.

coarse.meaning: Coarse describes a surface that feels harsh, or manners that are not polite.
coarse.clue: That material felt like sandpaper on my arms, and the man at the table spoke very rudely to the waiter.

coerce.meaning: To coerce somebody is to make them act by threat rather than by choice.
coerce.clue: The gang leader frightened the younger boys into handing over their pocket money, and the police arrested him.

coherent.meaning: A coherent account runs smoothly, because each point leads sensibly to the next.
coherent.clue: His explanation made sense from start to finish, even though the problem seemed impossible at first.

cohesive.meaning: A cohesive group fits together well, so it works as one rather than many parts.
cohesive.clue: Our football side plays as a single unit, and every player knows exactly what to do.

coincide.meaning: Two events coincide when they happen together, sometimes quite by chance.
coincide.clue: The school concert happened on the same evening as my birthday, so we joined the parties together.

collaborate.meaning: People collaborate when they share the work and the ideas for a project.
collaborate.clue: The two schools joined forces on the play, sharing costumes, scenery and the singing rehearsals.

collide.meaning: Things collide when they crash into one another, or when two views do not fit.
collide.clue: Two cars ran into each other at the roundabout, and the traffic stopped for nearly an hour.

colloquial.meaning: A colloquial word is the sort you use when talking with friends, not in an essay.
colloquial.clue: In the classroom we must choose careful words, not the everyday phrases we use with our friends.

collude.meaning: People collude when they quietly join forces to cheat someone together.
collude.clue: The two shopkeepers had been secretly fixing prices together, which is against the law.

combat.meaning: To combat something is to work hard against it, such as a disease or injustice.
combat.clue: The health team worked hard to stop the illness that had ruined the harvest for three summers.

combination.meaning: A combination is a set of different things used together for a single result.
combination.clue: Pairing the two colours gives a shade that neither of them had on its own.

comforting.meaning: Something comforting settles a worried person and makes them feel looked after.
comforting.clue: A warm blanket and a glass of milk help many small children settle after a bad dream.

comical.meaning: A comical scene is so silly or unexpected that it sets everyone laughing.
comical.clue: The clown lost his giant shoes and danced around in socks, and the crowd roared with laughter.

commemorate.meaning: To commemorate something is to mark it with a ceremony because it matters.
commemorate.clue: Every year the school holds a ceremony for the pupils who served in the wars.

commendable.meaning: Something commendable earns our approval because it was done carefully and with skill.
commendable.clue: The rescue team's quick thinking in the storm was admired by everyone who had watched the news.

commercial.meaning: A commercial organisation makes its money by selling things or providing a paid service.
commercial.clue: The station broadcasts adverts for shops and firms, which pays for the programmes we watch.

commit.meaning: To commit yourself to a promise means you will certainly see it through.
commit.clue: Once you have agreed to help with the show, you should stay and finish the job.

commotion.meaning: A commotion is a great deal of noise and excitement about something that has just happened.
commotion.clue: There was such a sudden hubbub in the corridor when the alarm rang that nobody heard the headteacher.

companion.meaning: A companion is someone who stays with you and keeps you company.
companion.clue: The new boy sits beside me at lunch, and we share our jokes and our sandwiches every day.

company.meaning: A company is a set of people in business, working together to make or sell things.
company.clue: The headteacher wrote to several companies in the town, hoping one would take on our four school leavers.

compel.meaning: If you compel someone to act, they do it because they have no real choice.
compel.clue: The heavy rain compelled us to cancel the picnic, so we played games indoors instead.

compile.meaning: To compile a list means gathering many separate items into a single set.
compile.clue: For our project we used ten books and put all the useful facts into a single report.

complacent.meaning: Being complacent means resting on your success and making no effort to get better.
complacent.clue: Our team rested on its early success and lost the final because nobody practised the new steps.
